solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Abrasive in having advantage over often luckless schemers

indicators.note: over signals the preceding piece turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, as in 'two up'
Burns's best-laid schemes of mice and men often go astray

explanation.surface: A sly remark about grinding something down in a scheme against unlucky plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns UP into PU; the schemers are the mice of Burns's poem 'To a Mouse', whose plans 'gang aft agley'.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic rock of this kind is used as a scouring stone, a classic household abrasive.

clue.text: Athena being cast in shadow

indicators.note: cast here means thrown off, so the following word is shed from the goddess's name

parts.note: Pallas is a title of the goddess Athena
as can mean being, in 'as a parent, I...'

explanation.surface: The goddess Athena is cast into darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' means thrown away: AS (being) is shed from PALLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pall is a dark covering cloud, as in a pall of smoke, which casts gloom like a shadow.

clue.text: Joe 90 occupied with creature of endless renown

parts.note: Joe, as in Joe Bloggs or Joe Public, is an ordinary man
XC is ninety in Roman numerals
at means busy with, as in 'at work'

explanation.surface: Joe 90, the puppet boy-agent of 1960s British TV, absorbed with some famous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless renown' puns on tail-less renown: this breed from the Isle of Man is famous for having no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is famed for lacking a tail, so its renown is literally about an end that is missing.

clue.text: Painter following companion to become political reformer

indicators.note: following puts the painter after the companion in the word

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: An artist tags along behind a friend and ends up in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists were nineteenth-century British campaigners for votes and parliamentary reform under the People's Charter.

clue.text: Wife, free to enter church after time, makes bit of history

indicators.note: to enter means the wife-and-free pair goes inside the other letters
after puts church behind time

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
W is wife, as in genealogies
open means free or unrestricted

explanation.surface: A wife is at liberty to go into church late, and so becomes part of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'to enter' both act here: one orders time and church, the other puts the wife pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth two old pennies belongs to pre-decimal British money, now a historical piece.

clue.text: Clift grinned — we hear wrong one to try charming women!

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of the preceding words put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the anagram despite looking like a sound signal

explanation.surface: Actor Montgomery Clift smirked, reportedly, at the wrong person for trying to charm women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a homophone signal but is just six letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Hopkins, called by that title, put supposed witches on trial in 1640s England; 'charming' means casting spells.

clue.text: Find fault with spirit that enters ancient Briton

indicators.note: that enters puts the spirit inside the ancient Briton

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
the ka is the ancient Egyptian spirit or soul

explanation.surface: A ghost possesses an early Briton and criticises him.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag at something with petty criticism is to carp, the same as finding fault.

clue.text: Flower arrangement for one covering chimney, black

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters sit around the rest
arrangement for signals the letters of 'one' rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
lum is Scots for a chimney
B is black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A flower arrangement placed over a sooty chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement for' shuffles 'one' into NEO, which goes 'covering' the rest; lum is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of the sacred lotus, a water plant with large blooms.

clue.text: Firm shows up to collect document with mistakes

indicators.note: to collect means the reversed word gathers the document inside it
in a down clue shows up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sure means firm or steady
a Roneo was a stencil duplicator, so a roneo is a copied document

explanation.surface: A company arrives to pick up some paperwork full of errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows up' reverses SURE to ERUS, which collects RONEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorrect is full of mistakes, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Like some ancient scripts amusing writer keeps at home

indicators.note: keeps means the writer holds the next piece inside

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse
in means at home

explanation.surface: A comic author stays home poring over old scripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear A and Linear B are ancient Aegean writing systems, so the adjective describes those scripts.

clue.text: One's less than flexible pole and feather duster?

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the poles
a feather duster can be used to tickle, so it is a tickler

explanation.surface: Something stiff, a pole, and a feather duster: an odd inventory of cleaning gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' wants to be a stick, but it is just the S of South.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insisting on strict rules is inflexible, a person who won't bend.

clue.text: Wily lochsman sits to fish

indicators.note: wily suggests twisting cunning, signalling the following words rearranged

explanation.surface: A crafty Highland loch-dweller settles down to angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link but its letters belong in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon from Scotland's rivers and lochs is a well-known kind of fish, a specific example.

clue.text: Angry miners set about MP drawing people into service

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the politician
angry suggests agitation, so the following letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Furious miners round on their Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' rearranges MINERS SET into IRESSMENT, which goes 'about' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: The press gang forcibly recruited men into the navy, conscription by force.

clue.text: Unsteady patients about to receive iodine treatment

indicators.note: to receive means the preceding letters take the element in
unsteady signals the letters of the next word wobbled into a new order

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Wobbly hospital patients are about to be given iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsteady' rearranges PATIENTS into ANTISEPT; with C added, I goes in before the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ-killing agent applied to wounds is a medical treatment, iodine being a familiar one.

clue.text: Self-loading washing-machine?

definitions.meaning: a gun that reloads itself between shots
a machine that runs its whole cycle unattended is called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: Both a self-reloading gun and an unattended washer run without hands-on operation.

clue.text: Sport in river, deep but not wide

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: but not means the next letter is left out

parts.note: low means deep, as a low voice
W is wide, the cricket extra

explanation.surface: Playing a game in a river that is deep but narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wide is a cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game played on horseback with mallets.

clue.text: Old tax collectors working towards same goal as sleuth

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority
on side means on the same team

explanation.surface: Former taxmen cooperating with a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Burr played the wheelchair-bound TV detective of this name, a fictional sleuth.

clue.text: Leader from Tarentum in the past pulled on this garment

indicators.note: leader from means the first letter of the next word
pulled suggests drawn back, so the next piece is read backwards

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A leader from the Roman-era city of Tarentum once put on this robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled' reverses the past-time word; 'this garment' points back to the Roman setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarentum was a Roman city and the toga was the citizen's robe, so 'this garment' fits the scene.

clue.text: See 5
Having no sex, Cagney actress gets closer in

indicators.note: in means the closer goes inside the actress's name

parts.note: Sharon Gless played Chris Cagney in the US TV series Cagney & Lacey
an ender is something that closes

explanation.surface: A TV actress comes nearer while sexless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as nearer but means one who ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Without gender is asexual, lacking male or female characteristics.

clue.text: New member has boozy natter with new resident

indicators.note: resident means the letter lives inside the rearranged word
boozy suggests a drunken jumble, so the next word's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A newcomer has a tipsy chat with a recently arrived local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozy' rearranges NATTER, and N is 'resident' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone just admitted to a club or contest is a newcomer, a fresh joiner.

clue.text: Persons from South African region importing books

definitions.note: the writer Truman Capote was born Truman Streckfus Persons, so the surname here is a person

indicators.note: importing means the region takes the books in

parts.note: the Cape is a region of South Africa
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: People from a part of South Africa bringing in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persons' looks like a plain plural, but it is the original surname of the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of In Cold Blood took his stepfather's surname; his birth surname was Persons.

clue.text: What chinless wonder wants is gift of sports psychology

definitions.meaning: mental means relating to the chin (Latin mentum), so a weak-chinned person lacks chin power
sports psychologists aim to give athletes resilience of mind

explanation.walkthrough: A 'chinless wonder' is British slang for a feeble upper-class twit; 'mental' also means of the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological toughness is what sports psychologists build, and the chin sense makes a pun.

clue.text: Expensive address for partner

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment used to a spouse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both costly and is a fond way of addressing a loved one.

clue.text: Shot through — as this, with cinnamon and raisins?

parts.note: a shot is a turn or go, as in 'have a shot'
over means finished, as in 'we're through'

explanation.surface: Something riddled through, the way a bun is studded with cinnamon and raisins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot through' reads as riddled, as a pastry filling runs through; split, it is two separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded pastry often filled with spiced apple and dried fruit fits a cinnamon-and-raisin bake.

clue.text: Anger appropriate to principal motorway an illusory thing

indicators.note: appropriate to means belonging with, so the anger is attached to the motorway's letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Road rage on Britain's main motorway is just an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its 1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion like water seen on a hot road is a deceptive vision.

clue.text: Gets beds back into chamber, but the other way around

indicators.note: into, with the clue's 'the other way around', means the chamber goes inside the beds

parts.note: cots are small beds

indicators.note: back means the chamber word is reversed

parts.note: a cell is a small chamber

explanation.surface: Someone shoves beds into a room, but backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the beds would be reversed into the chamber; 'but the other way around' swaps roles, so the chamber, turned 'back', sits in the beds.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather or fetch something is to obtain it, a synonym for getting.

clue.text: Gambler now attending Gamblers Anonymous?

definitions.meaning: someone in recovery is improving, on the mend

explanation.definitionFit: One who wagers, and also improved in health, as a recovering addict would hope to be.
